Validate Prepared Input Data

Source: R/validate_prepared_input.R
validate_prepared_input.Rd

Checks a prepared input table against the rules prep_data() enforces and reports how preparation will treat the data, without starting a run or writing anything to disk.

validate_prepared_input(
  input_data,
  combo_variables,
  target_variable,
  date_type,
  forecast_horizon,
  external_regressors = NULL,
  hist_start_date = NULL,
  hist_end_date = NULL,
  combo_cleanup_date = NULL,
  fiscal_year_start = 1,
  clean_missing_values = TRUE,
  forecast_approach = "bottoms_up",
  parallel_processing = NULL,
  back_test_scenarios = NULL,
  back_test_spacing = NULL
)

Arguments

input_data

A standard data frame, tibble, or spark data frame using sparklyr of historical time series data. Can also include external regressors for both historical and future data. Leading and trailing whitespace in character combo-variable values is removed before Finn creates internal series identifiers.

combo_variables

List of column headers within input data to be used to separate individual time series.

target_variable

The column header formatted as a character value within input data you want to forecast.

date_type

The date granularity of the input data. Finn accepts the following as a character string: day, week, month, quarter, year.

forecast_horizon

Number of periods to forecast into the future.

external_regressors

List of column headers within input data to be used as features in multivariate models. Controls built-in R1/R2 recipes only. C1 retains eligible original numeric, character, factor, logical and Date columns independently of this list in bottoms_up runs; hierarchical C1 nodes keep only these aggregated regressors. Each custom workflow uses only its declared predictors plus Date and Combo.

hist_start_date

Date value of when your input_data starts. Default of NULL uses earliest date value in input_data.

hist_end_date

Date value of when your input_data ends. Default of NULL uses the latest date value in input_data.

combo_cleanup_date

Date value to remove individual time series that don't contain non-zero values after that specified date. Default of NULL is to not remove any time series and attempt to forecast all time series.

fiscal_year_start

Month number of start of fiscal year of input data, aids in building out date features. Formatted as a numeric value. Default of 1 assumes fiscal year starts in January.

clean_missing_values

If TRUE, cleans missing values. Only impute values for missing data within an existing series, and does not add new values onto the beginning or end, but does provide a value of 0 for said values.

forecast_approach

Forecast approach, as passed to prep_data(). It is validated but does not change the checks: every approach expects bottom-level series, so totals mixed with their parts fail P7 for all.

parallel_processing

Default of NULL runs no parallel processing and forecasts each individual time series one after another. Value of 'local_machine' leverages all cores on current machine Finn is running on. Value of 'spark' runs time series in parallel on a spark cluster in Azure Databricks/Synapse.

back_test_scenarios

Number of back-test scenarios, as passed to prep_models(). Default of NULL chooses them from the history length.

back_test_spacing

Periods between back-test scenarios, as passed to prep_models(). Default of NULL uses the date type default.

Value

A list with:

  • passed: TRUE when no check failed.

  • checks: tibble with one row per rule and columns Rule, Description, Status ("pass", "fail", "report" or "skipped") and Message.

  • summary: list with the history start and end dates, row, series, history and future row counts, date_type and forecast_horizon.

  • details: list of tibbles and vectors behind the preparation checks: future_regressors, future_regressor_coverage, gaps, target_values, cleanup_combos, total_like_values, aggregate_levels, splits and short_history_combos.

Details

Input rules R1-R8, R10 and R11 reuse the checks in prep_data(), so a failure here carries the same message prep_data() would raise. R9 is stricter than prep_data(): it also checks that date_type matches the spacing of the dates. Preparation checks (P1-P8) describe what prep_data() and the train/test split planning will do with the data, such as future rows, padded gaps, missing values, series removed by combo_cleanup_date and short histories. A check fails only when the data cannot be prepared correctly; behavior that is applied automatically is returned with status "report".

Rules:

  • R1 combo variables, the target and external regressors exist.

  • R2 Date is not a combo variable, the target or an external regressor.

  • R3 the date column is named Date and has class Date.

  • R4 combo variables are not date columns.

  • R5 the target is numeric.

  • R6 combo values are not blank after trimming whitespace.

  • R7 each combo and Date pair appears once.

  • R8 month, quarter and year dates fall on one day of the month.

  • R9 date_type is valid and is not finer or coarser than the data.

  • R10 fiscal_year_start is a number from 1 to 12.

  • R11 Spark tables run with Spark parallel processing.

  • P1 history end date and the rows treated as future periods.

  • P2 external regressors with future values and their coverage.

  • P3 missing periods that preparation pads.

  • P4 missing, NaN and infinite target values.

  • P5 weekly dates share a weekday; quarterly and yearly dates share a period month.

  • P6 series removed by combo_cleanup_date.

  • P7 total or subtotal series mixed with the series they sum.

  • P8 history supports the forecast horizon and back-test splits.

Preparation checks run only when every input rule passes, and a check that depends on a failed check is skipped. Spark tables are collected locally after R11 is checked.

Examples

data_tbl <- timetk::m4_monthly %>%
  dplyr::rename(Date = date) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Date >= "2010-01-01")

result <- validate_prepared_input(
  input_data = data_tbl,
  combo_variables = "id",
  target_variable = "value",
  date_type = "month",
  forecast_horizon = 3
)

result$passed
